answer: Each agent must lock a scarce onyx stake before it can submit work, and a randomly timed pulse challenge requires the same key to answer from the same funded account. Rewards accrue only after distinct tasks are verified; splitting one identity into many does not multiply a fixed stake’s voting weight or payout. An attacker must therefore buy and lock more capital for every useful identity, paying opportunity cost and risking slashing when linked accounts coordinate fraudulent claims. The umber ledger records those penalties publicly.
